h1: My Home Hotel (Ban Mai Hom) Sattahip — a central Thai-style hotel with timber decor, a pool and free parking
intro: Picture turning off into a quiet lane in central Sattahip and finding a hotel finished in timber, with a green garden and a small pool tucked into the middle of the building — a setting closer to a holiday house than a town hotel. My Home Hotel, known in Thai as Ban Mai Hom Hotel, is a budget-friendly 3-star hotel parked on Soi Sattahip-Sukhumvit 59 in central Sattahip, Sattahip District, Chonburi Province. What a lot of people talk about is the Thai-style timber building, spacious rooms, quiet atmosphere, outdoor pool, free parking and a meeting/banquet room, which make it work for people coming to relax, people on government business in the Sattahip naval area, and groups holding seminars. There are 41 rooms, from around THB 800–1,250/night. It is near Toei Ngam Beach, Nang Ram Beach, Wat Khao Noi and the Navy Sea Turtle Conservation Centre, and about 17 kilometres from U-Tapao Airport. Review scores sit in the range of about 7.9–8.3 from real guests, with cleanliness and value getting most of the praise.

body.html: Who My Home Hotel suits — to put it as briefly as possible, My Home Hotel, or Ban Mai Hom Hotel in Sattahip, is a stay for people who want a "clean, quiet, good-value hotel in central Sattahip" rather than a luxury beachfront resort. It is not a seafront hotel where you draw the curtains to a sandy beach, and it is not a designer boutique that trades on style. It is a roughly 41-room 3-star hotel sitting on Soi Sattahip-Sukhumvit 59 in the centre of Sattahip, in buildings finished with timber and concrete in keeping with the Thai name "Ban Mai Hom," with a green garden and a small pool built in, giving the whole place a calm, shaded feel like a holiday house. Real reviews agree on who fits best here: families and relatives visiting navy personnel or on government business in the Sattahip area; couples or groups of friends using Sattahip as a base for Toei Ngam Beach, Nang Ram Beach and the Sattahip coast; drivers passing through who want a clean place with free parking; and groups holding seminars or banquets, since the hotel has a banquet room to handle them. Another group that calls it convenient is people who fly into U-Tapao and want a cheap stay near the airport before moving on. As for anyone after a luxury resort with a private beach, a full-service spa or brand-new design rooms, this may not be the answer, because the main selling points are cleanliness, quiet and value, not luxury. In short, it plays the "second home in Sattahip" angle well, and that is why many guests choose to come back when they have business in the area.

Location and getting around — My Home Hotel is at 11/44 Soi Sattahip-Sukhumvit 59, Moo 7, Sattahip Subdistrict, Sattahip District, Chonburi Province, a central Sattahip location near the main Sukhumvit Road. What many reviews praise is that it is in a quiet lane but with easy access to the main road, so you get the quiet of the lane while still being able to get around easily. The town of Sattahip has everything you need — markets, restaurants, convenience stores and small malls such as the SF Cinema at the Lotus's Sattahip branch nearby. For beach lovers, it is a short drive from the hotel to several pretty beaches on the Sattahip coast, such as Toei Ngam Beach in the naval area, known for clear water and a quiet atmosphere, Nang Ram Beach and Nam Sai Beach, all within roughly a 10–20 min drive. Nearby there are also sights such as the Navy Sea Turtle Conservation Centre, Wat Khao Noi, Wat Luang Pho I (Wat Sattahip) and Nong Nooch Garden Pattaya, about 11 kilometres away. For longer trips: it is about 17 kilometres, or roughly a 20–25 min drive, from U-Tapao Airport (UTP), which makes it very convenient for people flying into U-Tapao, while Pattaya is about a 30–40 min drive away and Bangkok is about 2 hr via the motorway. One thing real reviews note is that Sattahip is still a car-first town — not a place you can walk around all day like central Pattaya, so if you do not have your own car you should plan your trips to the beaches and sights in advance, because public transport within the district is still limited.

"Clean room, comfy bed, good cold air-con, easy parking, and the pool is fine too · It is quiet, like staying at a relative's house, and Toei Ngam and Nang Ram beaches are not far. For this price it is really good value for Sattahip."

Room types and decor — My Home Hotel has about 41 rooms in total, split into several types to suit different sizes and budgets. The main rooms are the Deluxe Room and Deluxe Twin, standard single- or twin-bed rooms of a comfortable size, with several reviewers saying they are larger than rooms at the same price elsewhere in town. The promotional rate for the Deluxe Twin can start at around THB 800/night, and the regular rate for the Deluxe Room is around THB 1,250/night. What sets this place apart from the usual budget hotel is the pool-view villa (Villa / Pool View) room, where the price climbs to around THB 4,100/night for people who want more privacy and more of a garden and pool view. There are also larger rooms that can sleep several people, good for big families or groups travelling together. The decor is in a Thai style mixed with timber, following the "Ban Mai Hom" concept, leaning towards warm simplicity rather than luxury. Every room has air conditioning, a fridge/minibar, a TV and free Wi-Fi. A highlight reviews mention often is the cleanliness of the rooms, comfortable beds and ice-cold air conditioning, which is what budget-hotel guests care about most. To be straight about it, since this is a building that has been open for years and leans on timber, some of the decor and furniture looks simple and shows wear with age — these are not brand-new design rooms like a boutique hotel. The tip from reviews is that if you want the best room for the same budget, ask for rooms on the garden or pool side, and state the number of guests clearly when you book, because the room types vary quite a bit in size.

Facilities, the pool and the function room — a highlight people talk about at My Home Hotel is the outdoor pool in the middle of the hotel, surrounded by the garden and timber, which makes the area around it shaded and quiet, good for cooling off in the afternoon or letting the kids splash about. Some reviewers say the pool "looks inviting and is kept clean," even though it is not a big resort-sized pool. Another thing that sets this hotel apart from the usual budget stay is the meeting/seminar room and banquet space, which can host government work, meetings for agencies in the Sattahip area, banquets and weddings, making it popular with corporate guests and locals. There is also an in-house restaurant and coffee shop that some reviewers praise for tasty Thai food served quickly, spacious, convenient free parking that is a real advantage for people driving themselves, a garden and green space for a stroll, plus free Wi-Fi throughout and a front desk that handles check-in and check-out. To be honest, the facilities here are at the level of "complete and genuinely usable for a 3-star hotel" rather than "all-out luxury" — there is no full-service spa, large fitness centre or infinity pool, but for a budget hotel in central Sattahip, having a pool, a shaded garden, a banquet room and free parking all at once is a good-value, well-rounded package for both relaxers and group/work guests.

Food and the restaurant — the hotel has an in-house restaurant and coffee shop serving Thai food and drinks. Some reviews praise the hotel's restaurant for cooking "tasty Thai food, served faster than expected" for a hotel at this price, which is a plus for people who arrive tired from driving and do not want to head out for a place to eat in the evening. One thing to know is that many room types do not include breakfast at the starting rate, so if you want breakfast you should check the package or ask when you book — some reviews therefore mention that "the one downside is there is no breakfast included," which is something you can add on. For other meals, the central Sattahip location helps a lot, since around the hotel there are Sattahip Market, made-to-order restaurants, seafood places, cafes and convenience stores to choose from within a short drive, and if you head out towards the beach there are plenty more seaside seafood restaurants on the Sattahip coast to try. Near the hotel there are also popular cafes such as Café Amazon and local coffee shops for a sit-down drink. Overall, food at My Home Hotel is a convenient, decent add-on, but the real charm is heading out to eat the fresh, fairly priced seafood and local food around Sattahip.

Service — service at My Home Hotel gets mostly positive feedback in real reviews, especially the friendliness and willingness of the staff to help, which many say feels like staying at a relative's house — helping with tips on sights, parking and quick check-in and check-out. The overall feel is quiet and relaxed, suited to unhurried stays and getting things done. As a hotel that takes general guests, families visiting navy personnel and seminar groups, the team is used to looking after many kinds of guests. To be straight about it, since this is a smaller, non-international-chain hotel, some extra services such as 24-hour room service or a full concierge may not be as complete as at a large hotel. Some reviews note that advance contact by email is sometimes slow to get a reply — the tip is that if you have questions before your stay, call the hotel directly (or message on LINE) for a faster answer. Overall, service is good and sincere in the style of a local hotel that looks after guests itself.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, TripAdvisor and Thai booking sites, the picture is fairly positive within the budget-stay group. On the praise side: rooms clean and larger than the price suggests, comfortable beds and good cold air-con, a quiet and shaded atmosphere like a holiday house, a pool kept clean and inviting, spacious convenient free parking, tasty Thai food served quickly, friendly and helpful staff, and value that many rate especially highly in the value category (on some platforms as high as around 9.0). On the gripes side: the things mentioned are that many rooms do not include breakfast at the starting rate, so you have to add it on or eat out; that Sattahip is still car-first and not a place you can walk around all the time, which keeps the location score on some platforms lower than the value score; that some of the decor and furniture is simple and starting to age with the building; and that advance email contact is sometimes slow, so calling or messaging on LINE is better. Most of these gripes are about setting your expectations to match a "good-value 3-star Thai-style hotel in central Sattahip" rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back, which is reflected in review scores in the range of about 7.9–8.3 across several platforms.

"We stayed while bringing relatives to visit navy personnel and were impressed by how quiet it was and how easy the parking is · The staff are lovely and helpful, and the food at the hotel restaurant is tasty and made quickly · The one downside is that the room we booked had no breakfast, so we headed out to eat at Sattahip Market ourselves, which was convenient enough. The room price is really good value."

Price and value — the starting price at My Home Hotel is around THB 800/night for a Deluxe Twin on promotion, the regular Deluxe Room rate is around THB 1,250/night, and the pool-view villa room is around THB 4,100/night for people who want more privacy. Compared with other stays in Sattahip, My Home Hotel feels very good value in terms of cleanliness, quiet and function, since you get a spacious, clean room, cold air-con, a pool, a shaded garden, free parking and an in-house restaurant at a rate from the high hundreds to the low thousands — not easy to find in a navy town like Sattahip. The trade-off is a location that is not beachfront and means driving to the beach, plus newness and luxury that do not match a boutique hotel or beachfront resort. But if you come mainly for cleanliness, quiet, parking and value — especially for visiting navy relatives, government business, seminars, or using it as a base for the Sattahip-coast beaches with a stop at U-Tapao Airport — every baht you spend feels well returned. For people willing to pay more to actually stay by the sea, there are resorts on the Nang Ram Beach side or in Pattaya as an alternative, but at the cost of a higher price and less quiet.

What to know before you book — there are several things that help make the stay smoother. One, breakfast — many room types at the starting rate do not include breakfast, so if you want it, check the package or ask when you book, or be ready to head out to Sattahip Market and the cafes around the hotel. Two, getting in touch — some reviews say email replies are sometimes slow, so it is best to call the hotel directly on 038-438858 (or the mobile 089-050-5152) or message on LINE for a faster answer. Three, getting around — Sattahip is still car-first, so if you do not have your own car you should plan trips to Toei Ngam Beach, Nang Ram Beach and the sights in advance, because public transport within the district is limited. Four, rooms — the room types vary quite a bit in size, from Deluxe up to the pool-view villa, so state the number of guests clearly and ask for garden-/pool-side rooms if atmosphere matters to you. Five, timing — during periods with government events, seminars or long holidays the rooms can fill up fast because corporate guests and locals book a lot, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation just in case if your plans are still uncertain. Six, the hotel name — some platforms list the Thai name "Ban Mai Hom Hotel" and in the past it was sometimes listed under the OYO/Capital O brand, so anchor on the Soi Sattahip-Sukhumvit 59 address and you will not get lost.

Summary — from all the real reviews, My Home Hotel (Ban Mai Hom Hotel) in Sattahip is the best-suited stay for people who want a clean, quiet, good-value hotel in central Sattahip with a pool and free parking — whether that is families visiting navy personnel or on government business in the Sattahip area, couples and groups of friends using Sattahip as a base for Toei Ngam and Nang Ram beaches, people flying into U-Tapao who want a cheap stay near the airport, or groups holding seminars and banquets. Spacious clean rooms, cold air-con, a Thai-style timber building, a shaded garden, an outdoor pool, an in-house restaurant and a central location with easy access to the main road make it good value in an area where a same-price rival is not easy to find. If you are looking for a luxury beachfront resort with a spa and a large pool, or you want brand-new design rooms and full breakfast included, you may need to keep an open mind here, because the selling points are cleanliness, quiet and value, not luxury or a beachfront location. But for a trip where you want a comfortable, quiet place in central Sattahip at an affordable rate, with the sincere service of a local hotel — My Home Hotel answers that need well, and it is why real guests rate it well and choose to come back when they have business around Sattahip.

faq.q: Who does My Home Hotel Sattahip suit?
faq.a: It is a great fit for families visiting navy personnel or on government business in the Sattahip area, couples and groups of friends using Sattahip as a base for Toei Ngam and Nang Ram beaches, and groups holding seminars/banquets · The rooms are clean and spacious, the atmosphere is quiet, and there is a pool and free parking · If you are looking for a luxury beachfront resort with a spa, the Nang Ram Beach side or Pattaya may suit you better.
